body:
`pr_idle_green` is the board's only PR-side obligation, and it requires
`.ci_failing == 0` by construction. `owe_reply` requires the last comment to be
someone else's. A contributor PR that is RED, whose last comment is OURS,
therefore matches no predicate at all and is invisible until
`needs_review_breach` fires at seven days.

That is the exact window in which the obligation is largest, because a red
contributor PR is owed an action either way: if we broke it, it is ours to fix;
if they broke it, it is ours to say so.

## Measured 2026-08-13 on #1488

@lduesing's OAuth auto-forward PR. On 08-09 we reviewed it, pushed three commits
to their branch, and told them the pending checks were only our Actions billing
lock -- "nothing for you to fix and no need to rebase".

The checks then ran on 08-10 and went red. `test_615_residual_i18n[fr]` and
`[nl]` failed on two msgids that **our own commit** `f3238ef` added to
`cps/spa_strings.py` without translations. The contributor's diff was never
implicated.

It then sat for 3.5 days. Board state at 16:11Z on 08-13 was
`never_acked=0 breaches=0 owe_reply=0` with the PR section reading 0, while
the person had been told the opposite of the truth and was waiting.

- `pr_idle_green`: false, `ci_failing` = 5.
- `owe_reply`: false, last comment was ours (08-09T18:34Z).
- `never_acked`: false, we had commented.
- `needs_review_breach`: would not fire until 08-17, seven days after 08-10.

## Fix

Add a `pr_idle_red` predicate beside `pr_idle_green`: `kind == "pr"`,
`author != self`, not draft, `ci_checks > 0`, `ci_failing > 0`, idle > 1 day.
Deliberately do **not** condition it on who authored the breaking commit --
that needs an extra API field and gets the disposition wrong in both
directions. Redness plus silence is the obligation, whoever caused it.

Related: F-8d8c15 (the board could not see PRs at all -- fixed 99b6cbc, which
is what made this narrower hole reachable).
title: A contributor PR that is red is invisible to the follow-up board
